summary: Task 08 complete (read-only investigation; no hardware writes, per parent directive). (1) blurswitchcs.dll metadata/string heaps fully recovered: it is a .NET 4.6.1 assembly whose AppService is `Lenovo.CameraControlBackgroundService` in UWP package family `E0469640.SmartAppearance_5grkq8ppsgwt4` — NOT `E0469640.LenovoUtility_5grkq8ppsgwt4` as STATE.md claimed (that string belongs to fnhotkeyutility.exe and is used to *activate* the LenovoUtility UWP app). Method set is exactly ToggleBlurSwitch / SendMessageAsync / OpenAsync on class BlurSwitchCS; status constants are STATUS_SET_BLUR_OFF_OK, STATUS_SET_BLUR_ON_OK, STATUS_EXCEPTION, STATUS_SVR_REPOND_ERR [sic], STATUS_SET_FEATURE_ERR, STATUS_RETURN_ERR, STATUS_CONNECT_SVR_ERR, STATUS_SET_TIMEOUT. Literals: "Key", "ToggleBlurSwitch", "Result", "BlurOff", "BlurOn", "BlurError". (2) dpinst.xml is a boilerplate DPInst wizard (only search/subDirectory + localized 'Energy Management Driver' text); lenovofnandfunctionkeys.cat is a PKCS#7 SignedData catalog listing every payload file, HWID acpi\lhk2019, signed by Microsoft Windows Hardware Compatibility Publisher — no .sys. Confirmed NO kernel-mode driver anywhere in package (glob **/*.sys empty; INF ServiceBinary = %13%\LenovoUtilityService.exe). (3) ludp.dll/ludp.net.dll/controllib.dll/intelcontrollib.dll/mmstate.dll/atiadlxx.dll contain ZERO camera/privacy/blur/LVF/SmartAppearance/AppService strings (only GPU-API noise in atiadlxx: ADL2_*Privacy/Camera_DMFT). (4) The switch STATE is never read/queried by these binaries; they only react to the WMI event payload bit (fnhotkey: `m_bExistRFDevice&8 pInfoData->Data[0]`, `SwitchCameraStatus in ....`) and only TOGGLE blur (BlurSwitchCS) / SET Windows camera privacy (pCameraControl[i]->Set). Deliverable contents are embedded in report because this agent has no write/exec tool. NOTE: ilspycmd could not be run (no shell tool in this agent's toolset) -> blurswitchcs.decompiled.cs is a metadata-accurate reconstruction, clearly flagged; main agent with bash should optionally confirm with `dotnet tool install -g ilspycmd && ilspycmd -t BlurSwitchCS <dll>`.

architecture: Payload = 'Lenovo Fn and function keys' 2.0.0.25 UMDF/user-mode package. INF binds ACPI device LHK2019 (DSDT Device HKDV, empty) -> installs auto-start Windows service `LenovoFnAndFunctionKeys` (ServiceBinary %13%\LenovoUtilityService.exe, SERVICE_OWN_PROCESS). LenovoUtilityService.exe launches FnHotkeyUtility.exe into the user session. FnHotkeyUtility subscribes to ROOT\WMI class LENOVO_UTILITY_EVENT, decodes the EC/firmware event (pInfoData->Data[0], m_bExistRFDevice bit 3) into e_Event_CAMERA_SWITCH_ON/OFF and, separately, e_Event_CAMERA_BG_BLUR; the latter calls BlurSwitchCLR.Switch() -> BlurSwitchCS.ToggleBlurSwitch() -> AppService Lenovo.CameraControlBackgroundService in UWP package E0469640.SmartAppearance_5grkq8ppsgwt4, which applies background blur and returns Result=BlurOn|BlurOff|BlurError. OSD is drawn by FnHotkeyUtility's own window. Windows camera privacy is SET (not read) via a COM camera-control moniker. No kernel-mode component exists in the package.
